$comment: THE OPEN / PAID BOUNDARY FOR THE INSTALLER PAYLOAD.
This file is the ONE place the boundary is written down. tools/check-payload-boundary.mjs
reads it and fails `npm run dist` if anything classified paid or excluded is present in
resources/capability, or if any payload file is classified nowhere at all.
STATUS IS "proposed". The classification below was drafted by the opensource-split-prep
lane from measurement, NOT decided by the owner. Everything under "pending" is a proposal
that is still shipping today; the guard names it on every build and does not fail on it.
Setting status to "owner-ratified" is refused while anything is still pending -- so
ratifying forces a decision on every open question rather than letting one be overlooked.
HOW THE OWNER EXPRESSES A DECISION: move a path out of "pending" into "open", "paid" or
"excluded". That is the whole edit. A path moved to paid or excluded turns the build RED
until the file genuinely stops being staged into the payload -- which, for anything
reachable from src/lib/tool-registry.js, means real decoupling work and not a config
change. See docs/design/OPEN-SOURCE-SPLIT.md section 4 for what that costs.
WHY "open" IS EXACT PATHS AND NEVER PREFIXES: a prefix classifies files that do not exist
yet, so a paid module dropped into an already-open directory next month would ship by
silence. Restrictive classes may use prefixes because over-matching there fails the build,
which is the safe direction to be wrong in.
MUST NOT SHIP AT ALL -- not an open-vs-paid question.
state/ is runtime spill: the mission bridge writes its per-boot bearer tokens there when
it is started out of the payload directory. Staging wipes the directory, so a clean
`npm run dist` never carries them -- but a payload copied by hand after any local run
does, and this rule is what catches that.
THE PATHS BELOW ARE DECOUPLED, NOT MERELY DECIDED. Each was moved out of `pending`
only after `npm run pack:capability` stopped staging it -- which for every one of them
meant removing a require() edge, not editing a list. Their tool definitions now live in
the capability source tree under src/lib/tool-packs/, loaded by the builder's own MCP
entry and by nothing the payload starts, so the packer's require() walk cannot reach
them. Listing a path here before that is true only turns the build red.
They are `excluded` rather than `paid` because they are not a product anyone could buy:
an identity-document pipeline reading one person's passport, and cloud routes that
commit by SHA256 to one person's Google Cloud account. Both are worthless to a stranger
and identifying to their owner.
PAID -- must never enter the public payload. These are not in it today. They are listed
so that the day someone adds a require() that pulls them into the closure, the build
stops here instead of publishing the paid enforcement path.

pending.src/lib/providers/chrome-web-store.js: OWNER DECISION 2026-08-11: NOT PART OF THIS PRODUCT -- excluded once decoupled; ships today. PROPOSE SPLIT (live identifier). Generic CWS upload/publish API client, but hardcodes AICALENDAR_STORE_ITEM_ID 'leodmhfokmdpdkbigklogdphlbkfahee' at line 15 and special-cases that one item. The generic half is publishable once the AICalendar branch is removed.
pending.src/lib/entitlement.js: OWNER DECISION 2026-08-11: PAID (ToolsEnabled Anywhere) -- still staged, so this entry moves out of pending only when the file genuinely stops shipping. PROPOSE PAID. Contains the actual commercial tier table and prices (community $0 / operator $19 / team $299, seatMinimum, productIds, hosted-relay grant). This is the business plan in source form.

PROPOSE PAID. Ed25519 licence-key issuance, verification and revocation -- the mechanism a paid tier is enforced with.

pending.src/lib/providers/firebase.js: OWNER DECISION 2026-08-11: NOT PART OF THIS PRODUCT -- excluded once decoupled; ships today. PROPOSE SPLIT (live identifier). Generic Firebase CLI wrapper plus a function hardcoding AICalendar's revenue Firebase project id 'aica-aed2a' (line 12). Generic half is publishable once that is removed.

$comment: PROPOSED OPEN. Derived from the measured staged payload, not hand-typed: every file the
packer stages that is not claimed above. Exact paths only.
FIVE OF THESE PATHS SHIP AS NEUTRAL DEFAULTS, NOT AS THE SOURCE FILE. config/agent-org.json,
config/managed-processes.json, config/model-floor.json, config/service-registry.json and
config/toolsenabled.policy.json are listed in tools/capability-manifest.json neutralDefaults,
so the packer stages capability-defaults/<path> in their place. This list classifies the bytes
that SHIP, which is what the guard walks -- the builder's own copies of those five are never
in the payload and are not classified by being here. Two of them were owner decisions to
SANITIZE rather than exclude: they are required at runtime, so removing them was never the
answer, and replacing them was.
